name: The Skinners
motto: You weren't using it right anyway.
description:
The Skinners are exactly what the name implies. They're a crew of roughly twenty-five augment strippers working the back alleys and underpasses of Cleveland's Flats district, and their business model is simple: find someone with valuable cyberware, take it out of them, sell it. The extraction process ranges from crude to clinical depending on which Skinner is holding the blade and how cooperative the victim is. Some targets wake up in a bathtub missing a cybernetic arm. Others don't wake up at all.

What distinguishes the Skinners from common muggers is their technical competence. The crew includes three former augment technicians — people who worked in legitimate clinics before the industry consolidated and automated their jobs away. These technicians can remove implants without killing the host, most of the time, and can assess the value of installed cyberware at a glance. They've developed a system: scouts identify targets with valuable chrome, trackers follow them to isolation points, and the extraction team moves in with surgical tools and stun weapons. It's efficient, professional, and deeply horrifying.

The Skinners sell their harvest through a network of black-market buyers, chop shops, and gray-market clinics that don't ask where their inventory comes from. A clean military-grade cybernetic limb can fetch enough to keep the crew fed for a month. Neural interfaces are worth more. Optical augments, less — too many compatibility issues. The Skinners know the market and they price accordingly.

The crew is feared and hated in equal measure. Even other criminals consider them predatory. The Iron Lotus has put bounties on Skinners who operate in the Gray Zone territory without permission. Axiom Security occasionally makes a show of cracking down on augment theft, though never with enough commitment to actually stop it.
ideology: Pure profit motive with a thin veneer of class resentment. The Skinners tell themselves they're redistributing chrome from people who can afford replacements to people who can't afford originals. Some of them might even believe it. Mostly, they're in it for the money.
territory: Cleveland's Flats district and the surrounding industrial waterfront. Hunting ground extends throughout Cleveland's lower wards.
methods: Target identification — scouts with optical augments scan crowds for valuable cyberware
Tracking and isolation — following targets to vulnerable positions away from witnesses or security
Forced extraction — stun weapons, restraints, and surgical tools used to remove augments from unwilling donors
Technical assessment — former clinic technicians evaluate and grade stolen cyberware for resale
Black-market distribution — a network of buyers, chop shops, and gray clinics purchasing stolen chrome
Intimidation — the Skinners' reputation itself is a weapon that keeps victims from fighting back
resources: Three former augment technicians with legitimate surgical skills
Surgical tools and portable extraction equipment
A network of black-market buyers across the GLMZ
Scout teams with optical augments optimized for identifying cyberware models
A rotating series of extraction sites — abandoned buildings rigged as temporary operating rooms
Stun weapons and chemical sedatives for subduing targets
story_hooks: The Skinners stripped chrome from someone connected — now a syndicate wants the crew eliminated and the augments returned
A Skinner defector wants protection in exchange for the crew's client list — buyers who knowingly purchase stolen augments
The Skinners accidentally extracted an augment containing encrypted corporate data — now they're a target
Someone is hiring the Skinners to strip specific targets, turning them into a precision weapon against augmented operatives
A victim of the Skinners is hiring a freelancer for revenge, but the target Skinner has information that complicates the job
